assumptions.description: All zero/minus/plus labels use identical admitted Oh PMC6911291.1 and Bansal publisher snapshot, evidence bytes, source covariates, replay recipes, measurement mapping and semantic definitions. Summaries share study participants; repeated rows/seeds are not independent clinical evidence. No real target outcomes are available.

Oh source context has 160320 synthetic rows: 60 times each published sex count. Within each sex, age and BMI are generated separately from maximum-entropy discrete marginal distributions constrained by Table 1 mean/SD and Table 2 stratum counts. Assumed age support 18..85 years and BMI grid 14..45 at 0.05 spacing. Entropy is relative to a uniform grid within each reported stratum. Quantile allocation and independent fixed-seed permutations approximate independence of age and BMI conditional on sex. The joint distribution, tails and family links are unreported; independence is a working approximation, not a discovered fact.

Bansal fasting context has 80472 synthetic women (4 times 20118). Age is 45 plus a gamma distribution with excess mean 9.5 and SD 7.2, rounded to integer years and capped at 120 solely to satisfy task support. BMI is lognormal with arithmetic mean 25.9 and SD 5.0. Deterministic stratified marginal quantiles are independently permuted using the one fixed context seed. Age-BMI dependence, hormone use, medication and other risk factors are unknown. TG tertile-specific age/BMI summaries are diagnostics only and are not used to construct covariates conditional on an assigned TG outcome.

All source rows use legacy_proxy and checks use identity mg/dL mapping. Bansal explicitly corrected endogenous glycerol, supporting a glycerol-blanked proxy; Oh reports Cobas 6000 but not glycerol blanking, so its equivalence is weaker and assumed. Both used EDTA plasma, whereas target is fasting serum LBXTLG. Neither source proves equivalence to the exact old NHANES assay. This uncertainty remains common to all structures.

The task-supplied forward equation 12.45 + 1.022 * legacy_proxy TG is applied only to unblanked_2021_2023 rows. It is measurement context, not target-population association evidence. The point equation is treated deterministically because no coefficient covariance is supplied here. It does not establish interchangeability or alter age/BMI/sex biology; backward sensitivity is controlled elsewhere.

Bansal does not report its quantile interpolation convention. Source replay uses explicitly typed linear (Hyndman-Fan type 7) sample quantiles as an approximation, retaining reported 81, 115 and 169 mg/dL without converting them.

Continuous TG is compared with Oh thresholds 150, 200 and 500 mg/dL. Oh Table 1 says >500 while prose says 500 and up; a continuous draw has zero exact-threshold mass. For Bansal integer-labeled tertiles and quintiles, half-unit boundaries 90.5/147.5 and 73.5/98.5/132.5/184.5 approximate rounding to reported integer mg/dL. Cumulative proportions are derived from published counts; these preserve every category count without pretending the bins are exact quantile probabilities.

Oh Table 3 reports age/sex-adjusted simple linear BMI regression. The source replay estimates ordinary unweighted OLS TG~age+sex+BMI with intercept; sex is coded 1 male, 2 female and the BMI coefficient is invariant to reference coding. Family weighting/correlation and exact analysis details are unavailable, so this is approximate. Table 4 additionally adjusted metabolic model, Table 5 mixed lifestyle model, and Table 6 co-twin estimands are not substituted for Table 3.

Oh Table 2 TG summaries have no explicit arithmetic/geometric label and methods mention geometric averages. Count-weighted BMI strata reconstruct 141.5937/97.2021 and age strata 141.6062/97.2153 mg/dL, supporting an arithmetic reading but not resolving contradictory wording. They are retained as reported_other with no arithmetic replay. Only qualitative shape motivates assumptions; no summary is relabeled as a verified conditional arithmetic mean.

The generator has only age, sex and BMI as biological predictors. Missing medication, hormonal, diet, alcohol, diabetes, ancestry and family variables are integrated into individual residual variation or a latent state without claiming their actual values or conditional independence in real populations. Neither a nonsignificant result nor an absent association is evidence of zero.

This task appends TG to a synthetic age/sex/BMI grid only. It makes no target-population validity claim. The two source contexts retain their distinct population/selection/measurement limitations. The source-derived biological law is applied uniformly without cohort/assay/ID selectors; any use outside a reported source population remains an unverified transport assumption.

Fixed source covariates and scientific parameters; source seeds78101,78102,78103 and synthetic probe seeds78201,78202,78203 vary individual residual draws. The paired inverse-CDF uses the same original normal draw without new RNG draws. Source seed variation is Monte Carlo variation, not source-study confidence, structural uncertainty or population-transfer uncertainty. All three labels and scheduled seeds are retained.

The base f0 is the s1_final additive conditional arithmetic mean with sex-specific BMI/linear age slopes, smooth positive floor and mean-one lognormal residual. zero uses exactly f0. minus/plus add a compact male density interaction described in A_density_interaction. This changes age-BMI-TG three-way dependence under an explicitly assumed product source covariate law while preserving both bivariate outcome laws in population. It is a sensitivity construction, not a reported mechanism.

After complete initial source-only feedback, choose a female BMI slope 5.2 mg/dL per kg/m^2 as an explicit sensitivity to overstated Bansal BMI rank and tertile separation. This is not a reported or identified coefficient. Balance the unreported male slope using published sex counts and BMI variances so their variance-weighted pooled coefficient is 6.813 under the fixed independent-within-sex source context. Recalculate residual CV algebraically to keep the same marginal mean/SD anchors. Keep age slopes unchanged because its reverse-conditional age summaries give conflicting guidance. The change can worsen Bansal location/quantiles; no numerical improvement is claimed before replay.

The exact historical source-only anchor code/spec/evidence/recipe hashes and actual source-feedback report are bound. This anchor has documented source mismatches, including Bansal quartiles and age Spearman; invariance preserves rather than repairs them. No winning or clinically valid status is inferred.

f_t=f0+t*delta*hA(age)*hB(BMI)*hT(TG) for men only. Compact bases are zero outside declared interior source-support regions and marginally centered using fixed source covariates. Integral(hT)=0 ensures per-person normalization. Independent source age/BMI makes both age-TG and BMI-TG laws invariant; finite independently permuted source rows are not exactly a product law. Unknown real-source dependence and missing covariates remain limitations. Sign labels denote density directions only; no desired outcome sign or target coefficient is supplied.

delta is the fixed pre-execution design value .07077021813077161, obtained as .8*50 times the analytically endpoint-certified minimum male f0 density on the compact support. The bound gives .2*f0<=f_t<=1.8*f0 on kernel support and equality elsewhere. Certificate includes complete formulas/corners; this is not a grid-minimum claim or a source-estimated amplitude.

Use the anchor normal draw to define its uniform CDF value; invert F0+t*delta*hA*hB*H on[70,190] with40bisectionsteps using stdlib math.erf and NumPy. All other rows retain their baseline draw exactly. Analytic final interval width120/2^40 is separate from ordinary floating-point error; no runtime success is claimed before isolated execution.

Prespecified analytical materiality is max absolute E_plus(TG|age,BMI,sex=1)-E_minus over age40/60 and BMI23/27, at least5mg/dL. Fixed parameters give max9.907830538308025mg/dL at60/27. Not every cell must exceed5. This is a diagnostic model-separation threshold, not clinical importance, inferential certainty or a desired target regression sign.

Oh Table2 age/BMI values remain unresolved arithmetic/geometric evidence. semantic_metrics.json declares both interpretations and explicit interval approximations, to be computed only from verified source replay output. Both bivariate distributions are invariant under the product population regardless of estimator interpretation, but anchor discrepancies and finite-context deviations remain. Other adjusted/family estimands remain unassessed; lack of operators does not remove them.

structure_id.derivation: Three fixed sensitivity labels share one anchor and one compact interaction family; no model probabilities or target-result ranking.

reference.derivation: Reported Oh sex-specific marginal moments. They are centering and spread anchors, not individual conditional values. Order is male, female.

assay.derivation: Task-supplied technical equation; not counted as an approved biological evidence source.

bmi_slope.derivation: Female 5.2 is a deliberately rounded source-conditioned assumption motivated by initial Spearman .439490 vs .33 and excessive reverse-conditional BMI separation; not a conversion of Spearman to a slope. Male=(6.813-(1-w)*5.2)/w=9.55730972758, w=(1029*3.1^2)/(1029*3.1^2+1643*3.2^2)=0.370182544011. Published Table 2 qualitative sex difference motivates allowing heterogeneity without resolving its summary-type ambiguity. Algebra preserves the pooled source slope only under the declared approximate source covariate construction; actual replay remains required.

age_slope.derivation: Chosen mild male decrease and female increase in mg/dL/year reflect reported sex-specific age shapes; not obtained by replacing marginal Spearman with a coefficient. The female linear slope smooths the stronger middle-age transition.

residual_cv.derivation: Reapply the original analytic independent-covariate moment formula using revised sex-specific BMI slopes and unchanged age slopes: Var(mu)=bBMI(sex)^2 Var(BMI)+bAge(sex)^2 Var(age); CV^2=(reportedTGVar-Var(mu))/(reportedMean^2+Var(mu)). No final generator or simulated TG moments were computed by the builder.

positive_mean.derivation: Assumed smooth positive regularization floor+width*log(1+exp((linearMean-floor)/width)); avoids negative means at unsupported covariate extremes. It is not a TG truncation or observed lower bound.

density_interaction.derivation: All bounds, bands, materiality threshold and safety fraction were specified before execution. Source-only marginal counts set compact centering fractions; analytic endpoint positivity sets fixed delta. Sign is the only numerical difference among the three specifications. Parameters are scientific sensitivity assumptions, not estimated source coefficients or uncertainty.
